report_name: Elsevier Domains Hijacked to Redirect to LAPSUS$ Extortion Page

threat_actors.name: LAPSUS$
threat_actors.description: Branding used in a domain hijacking incident against Elsevier. The malicious redirect page was branded 'LAPSUS$ GROUP, Chapter II'. Security researchers note there is no confirmed link to the original LAPSUS$ group, suggesting a copycat actor.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: The attackers likely gained access to Elsevier's DNS provider or Content Delivery Network (CDN) account via compromised credentials to modify traffic routing rules.

attack_patterns.name: Domains
attack_patterns.description: One of the potential attack vectors was DNS hijacking, where the attacker compromised Elsevier's domain registrar or DNS hosting account to change A or CNAME records.

attack_patterns.name: Modify Cloud Compute Configurations
attack_patterns.description: One of the potential attack vectors was CDN hijacking, where the attacker compromised Elsevier's account with their CDN provider (reportedly Cloudflare) and created a redirect rule to hijack traffic.

identities.name: Elsevier
identities.description: Major academic publisher whose domains (Elsevier.com, Evolve.elsevier.com, and submit.elsevier.com) were temporarily hijacked and redirected to a malicious page.

identities.name: FBI
identities.description: The US Federal Bureau of Investigation was taunted on the malicious redirect page set up by the attackers.

identities.name: Cloudflare
identities.description: The CDN provider reportedly used by Elsevier, whose configuration may have been compromised to execute the domain hijacking via a modified redirect rule.

infrastructure.name: LAPSUS$ Hijack Redirect Page
infrastructure.description: An external webpage branded with the LAPSUS$ name that taunted the FBI. It was the destination of an HTTP 302 redirect from the hijacked Elsevier domains for at least 78 minutes.
